subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The following table shows the frequency distribution of the time required for each worker to complete a work. From the table find the mean time required to complete the job for a worker.

| Time (Hrs.) for each to complete the work | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-29 | 30-34 | 35-39 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of workers | 10 | 15 | 12 | 8 | 5 |
solution:
The mean is found by the direct method. Note that the class mark of a class is not changed by making the classes continuous, so the printed classes may be used as they are.

| Class (Time in hrs.) | Class mark \(x_i\) | Frequency (No. of workers) \(f_i\) | \(x_i f_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15-19 | 17 | 10 | 170 |
| 20-24 | 22 | 15 | 330 |
| 25-29 | 27 | 12 | 324 |
| 30-34 | 32 | 8 | 256 |
| 35-39 | 37 | 5 | 185 |
| Total | | \(\Sigma f_i = 50\) | \(\Sigma x_i f_i = 1265\) |

Mean \(= \overline{X} = \dfrac{\Sigma x_i f_i}{N} = \dfrac{1265}{50} = 25.3\)   ... \(\because \Sigma f_i = N\)

\(\therefore\) the mean time required to complete the work for a worker \(= 25.3\) hrs. (approx.)

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The percentage of marks of 50 students in a test is given in the following table. Find the mean of the percentage.

| Percentage of marks | 0-20 | 20-40 | 40-60 | 60-80 | 80-100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of students | 3 | 7 | 15 | 20 | 5 |
solution:
The following table is prepared by the direct method.

| Class (Percentage of marks) | Class mark \(x_i\) | Frequency (No. of students) \(f_i\) | \(x_i f_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-20 | 10 | 3 | 30 |
| 20-40 | 30 | 7 | 210 |
| 40-60 | 50 | 15 | 750 |
| 60-80 | 70 | 20 | 1400 |
| 80-100 | 90 | 5 | 450 |
| Total | | \(\Sigma f_i = 50\) | \(\Sigma x_i f_i = 2840\) |

Mean \(= \overline{X} = \dfrac{\Sigma x_i f_i}{\Sigma f_i} = \dfrac{2840}{50} = 56.8\)

\(\therefore\) the mean of the percentage of marks is \(56.8\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The maximum temperatures in \(^\circ\)C of 30 towns, in the last summer, is shown in the following table. Find the mean of the maximum temperature.

| Temperature (\(^\circ\)C) | 24-28 | 28-32 | 32-36 | 36-40 | 40-44 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of towns | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 6 |
solution:
| Class (Temp. \(^\circ\)C) | Class mark \(x_i\) | Frequency (No. of towns) \(f_i\) | \(x_i f_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24-28 | 26 | 4 | 104 |
| 28-32 | 30 | 5 | 150 |
| 32-36 | 34 | 7 | 238 |
| 36-40 | 38 | 8 | 304 |
| 40-44 | 42 | 6 | 252 |
| Total | | \(\Sigma f_i = 30\) | \(\Sigma x_i f_i = 1048\) |

Mean \(= \overline{X} = \dfrac{\Sigma x_i f_i}{\Sigma f_i} = \dfrac{1048}{30} = 34.93\)

\(\therefore\) the mean of the maximum temperature is about \(34.9\ ^\circ\)C.

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The following table shows the funds collected by 50 students for flood affected people. Find the mean of the funds.

| Fund (Rupees) | 0-500 | 500-1000 | 1000-1500 | 1500-2000 | 2000-2500 | 2500-3000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of students | 2 | 4 | 24 | 18 | 1 | 1 |
solution:
If the number of scores in two consecutive classes is very low, it is convenient to club them. So the classes 0-500, 500-1000 are clubbed, and so are 2000-2500, 2500-3000. The new table is:

| Fund (Rupees) | 0-1000 | 1000-1500 | 1500-2000 | 2000-3000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of students | 6 | 24 | 18 | 2 |

Let \(A = 1250\); examining all the \(d_i\)'s, \(g = 250\).

| Class (Fund) | Class mark \(x_i\) | \(d_i = x_i - 1250\) | \(u_i = \dfrac{d_i}{g}\) | Frequency \(f_i\) | \(f_i u_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1000 | 500 | \(-750\) | \(-3\) | 6 | \(-18\) |
| 1000-1500 | 1250 | 0 | 0 | 24 | 0 |
| 1500-2000 | 1750 | 500 | 2 | 18 | 36 |
| 2000-3000 | 2500 | 1250 | 5 | 2 | 10 |
| Total | | | | \(\Sigma f_i = 50\) | \(\Sigma f_i u_i = 28\) |

\(\overline{u} = \dfrac{\Sigma f_i u_i}{\Sigma f_i} = \dfrac{28}{50} = 0.56\)

\(\overline{u}\,g = 0.56 \times 250 = 140\)

\(\overline{X} = A + g\,\overline{u} = 1250 + 140 = 1390\)

\(\therefore\) the average of the funds is ₹ 1390.
